## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Asātarāgakathā* is a debate text situated within the thirteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The controversy addresses the proposition that there exists a "lusting for what is disagreeable" (*asātarāga*), a doctrine attributed to the Uttarāpathakas [Dube 1980]. The orthodox Theravādin tradition countered that the Uttarāpathakas derived this proposition from a misunderstood canonical statement [Dube 1980]. Modern scholarship notes that the Uttarāpathakas appear to have developed this position from an experiential psychological observation—specifically, the phenomenon wherein fascination is exercised by objects in which disagreeable elements predominate, exemplified by a person prone to sudden rage who actively enters into a brawl [Dube 1980].

Furthermore, DharmaNexus highlights shared phrasing with other *Kathāvatthu* chapters, such as the *Aññāṇakathā* (Kv 2.2), *Parūpahārakathā* (Kv 2.1), and *Antarābhavakathā* (Kv 8.2), while recording no cross-language matches meeting the score threshold [DharmaNexus].
